messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P99 latency SLO breach for cont-batch path in us-west-2. Alert threshold: 750ms, current P99 ~1.3s; start=1976543160. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming enabled), /v1/chat (cont-batch). Incident severity: P2.

Erin (oncall): acked. Paging in progress. Anyone oncall here? @Mike (rt) can you pull the p95/p99 breakdown and top hosts?

Mike (rt): I'm on. dashboards -> https://graf.redwood/p/latency/cont-batch?org=platform
Mike (rt): quick snapshot: p95=220ms, p99=1300ms, tail spikes concentrated on cont-batch worker pool gw-cb-usw2-*. CPU fine, gpu util ~65%, but queue_time histogram shows long wait (0.4-1.1s) for many requests.

Erin (oncall): thanks. Any streaming stalls too? Customers reporting chunked responses. @Liz any customer escalations?

Liz (cs): got 2 SEV2s from customers on dev keys — intermittent 5-10s stalls on streaming responses. They're able to retry but worried about quality degradation. Tracking customers A and B.

Raj (sre): looking at trace samples from X-Ray. Pattern: mixed-seqlen requests (short prompt + very long user message) are being packed into same batch, causing KV cache growth + paging overhead and blocking the streaming goroutine. Scheduler fairness looks skewed: large sequences get priority to fill batch and hold GPU for 800-1200ms. Attached trace ids: trace-7f3a, trace-8a2b.

Ana (prod-eng): that matches our cont-batch path hypothesis — large mixed sequences + continuous batching -> head-of-line blocking. Two short-term mitigations: 1) cap max_batch_size for cont-batch pool to 96 (was 256) 2) enable preemptive_batch_shedding on gw-cb nodes so streaming requests can preempt large batches. Long-term: better sequence-length aware packing and fairshare scheduler.

Erin (oncall): propose emergency mitigations now. Mike, can you run a canary with reduced batch cap and preemptive flag on one host group?

Mike (rt): prepping change. command: ```
# canary change
redwoodctl update-pool --pool gw-cb-usw2-canary --max-batch-size 96 --set preemptive_batch_shedding=true
```
Mike (rt): deploy-bot: deploying to gw-cb-usw2-canary (3 nodes).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for gw-cb-usw2-canary -> nodes: canary-1, canary-2, canary-3. CI checks passed.

Mike (rt): canary metrics after 2m: p99 on canary nodes dropped from ~1.2s to ~420ms; queue_time 95th dropped from 800ms -> 140ms. No errors.

Raj (sre): good signal. We should also reduce KV cache TTL on canary to evict oversized contexts faster: ```
redwoodctl set-config kv_cache.ttl=30s --pool gw-cb-usw2-canary
```

Ana (prod-eng): also suggest routing streaming sessions to dedicated streaming pool to avoid cont-batch scheduling entirely for them. Config snippet: ```
routing.rules.add(name="prefer-streaming-pool", match="request.streaming=true", dest_pool="gw-stream-usw2")
```

Erin (oncall): roll canary to 50% of cont-batch capacity if metrics hold. Mike, Raj coordinate. Liz keep CS updated.

Mike (rt): rolling to 50% now. command: ```
redwoodctl rollout-pool --from gw-cb-usw2-canary --to gw-cb-usw2 --percent 50
```

deploy-bot: Rollout at 50% complete. Monitoring.

Mike (rt): after 10m at 50%: cluster-wide p99 dropped to 540ms, streaming stalls reports reduced, error rate steady. Good.

Raj (sre): adding temporary scheduling tweak to fairness weights: ```
scheduler.set-weight(seq_len_bucket=short, weight=1.5)
scheduler.set-weight(seq_len_bucket=long, weight=0.8)
```

Ana (prod-eng): we need to be careful — lowering long weight could increase throughput loss for long-batched workloads. We'll bake a config that ties weight to latency SLO.

Erin (oncall): any customer still seeing tail issues? Liz?

Liz (cs): Customer A reports improvement, Customer B intermittent but better. They're OK with us continuing rollout.

Mike (rt): finishing 100% rollout now. command: ```
redwoodctl rollout-pool --from gw-cb-usw2-canary --to gw-cb-usw2 --percent 100
```

deploy-bot: Rollout complete. Post-rollout CI smoke passed.

Mike (rt): final metrics 20m after mitigations: p95=180ms, p99=420ms, request_timeouts down 92%. Streaming stall rate down ~88%.

Erin (oncall): closing immediate pager. Logging incident as P2. Notes: cause = cont-batch scheduling fairness + mixed sequence length packing causing head-of-line blocking; mitigations = reduce max_batch_size to 96; enable preemptive_batch_shedding; temporary scheduler weight adjustments; route streaming to dedicated pool; KV cache TTL lowered.

Ana (prod-eng): action items for postmortem: - implement sequence-length aware packing (owner: Ana) - add routing rule by streaming flag permanently (owner: Mike) - update runbooks and add synthetic tests with mixed-seqlen traffic (owner: Raj) - revert KV TTL change after follow-up if not needed (owner: Mike).

Raj (sre): I'll capture traces and add to postmortem. Also recommend an alert tweak: split cont-batch p99 per-seqlen-bucket so we surface this earlier.

Erin (oncall): handing off to next oncall @Maya. Summary: incident resolved -> mitigations in prod; monitoring in place; postmortem owners assigned. Full context in incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1976543210.

Maya (oncall-next): acked, thanks. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if regressions show up. Can you drop any runbook edits into #eng-oncall-runbooks and ping me?

Erin (oncall): will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Liz (cs): sending update to affected customers now.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-322 created and linked to thread.

Erin (oncall): closing thread — will start postmortem doc tomorrow.
